reflection_oracle_classification: I classified the oracle as balanced because the seeded mask [1, 0, 1, 1] contains at least one 1, so the function depends on the input parity. The output_offset is 0 here, but even if it were 1 it would only flip every oracle output and would not change the constant/balanced classification.
reflection_bit_order: The measurement map is reversed: q0->c3, q1->c2, q2->c1, and q3->c0. The mask is written in q[0]...q[3] order, while Qiskit displays counts in c[3]...c[0] order, so the expected logical string 1101 is displayed as 1011.
reflection_hardware_noise: I did not run the optional IBM hardware extension. On real hardware I would expect the ideal 1011 outcome to remain prominent but to be accompanied by other bitstrings because of gate errors, readout errors, decoherence, and imperfect two-qubit operations. Therefore the hardware distribution would usually be less concentrated than the ideal simulator result, and exact hardware counts should not be expected to match the simulator.
